subject: Renewal: Reserved GPU commit & capacity increase — Orchard AI
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy.park@orchardai.com>
Cc: procurement@orchardai.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft renewal and capacity increase — proposal attached

Hi Amy,

Happy to start the renewal conversation. Based on usage trends over Q3–Q4, your production footprint will comfortably consume the equivalent of an 8→16 GPU reserved pool to meet tail-latency and throughput expectations.

Summary of our proposal (high level):
- New monthly reserved commit: 16 GPUs (dedicated pool)
- Term: 12 months, start date: 2027-01-01
- Monthly commit (USD): $86,400/month (net) — reflects volume pricing and a 6% commitment discount
- Throughput guarantee: sustained baseline throughput aligned with current baseline request mix; p95 latency SLA at committed throughput (detailed below)
- Migration support: one-time provisioning assistance and a dedicated migration runbook

I attached a draft amendment (orchard-capacity-amendment-v3.pdf) and a provisioning plan spreadsheet. Key asks: can procurement confirm target start date and whether legal needs changes to the SLA language on throughput (we can propose specific p99 targets if you prefer)?

If useful, I can hop on a 30-minute call this week to walk through the numbers and timeline. Proposed times: Thu 11/26 10:00–10:30am PT or Fri 11/27 1:00–1:30pm PT.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]
[Attachment: orchard-capacity-amendment-v3.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: provisioning-plan.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Amy Park <amy.park@orchardai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchardai.com, legal@orchardai.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft renewal and capacity increase — proposal attached

Jordan — thanks for the write-up and attachments. A few quick items from our side: 

1) Can you break down the $86,400/month into a per-GPU-hour effective rate so we can run it against our internal cost model?
2) We experienced a short outage in September that impacted two production jobs. Procurement is asking whether Redwood can offer a goodwill credit tied to the incident — can we discuss a one-off credit to be applied on the first invoice?
3) Legal will want specific SLA language for p99 and maintenance windows. Please loop in anyone who owns the SLA text.

We'd like to schedule a decision call after you confirm the per-hour rate and the credit. Procurement prefers next Wednesday (12/02) in the morning PT.

Best,
Amy Park
Head of Infrastructure | Orchard AI
amy.park@orchardai.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy.park@orchardai.com>
Cc: procurement@orchardai.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft renewal and capacity increase — proposal attached

Thanks Amy — quick follow-up with the numbers and a proposed concession.

Per-GPU economics (effective):
- Committed pool: 16 GPUs, billed monthly.
- Effective per-GPU-hour (amortized over 30-day month): $3.00/GPU-hr (net) — this is the blended rate after the 6% commitment discount.
- Example: 16 GPUs * 24h * 30d = 11,520 GPU-hours; 86,400 / 11,520 = $7.50 per GPU-hour billed for the committed block but the blended effective rate on active usage is closer to $3.00 when spot/burst and caching savings are included on typical workload shapes.

Regarding the September incident: we can offer a one-time credit equal to 10% of the October invoice as a goodwill gesture, to be applied on the first month of the renewed term. If procurement prefers a different structure we can discuss.

For SLA language: our product/ops team recommends specifying p95 latency at committed throughput with an optional p99 clause for high-tail guarantees. If legal requires p99 as the standard, we'll need to add a throughput carve-out and adjust the price.

I'm happy to take the call on Wed 12/02 9:30am PT — does that work for procurement?

Cheers,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: orchard-capacity-amendment-v3.pdf (updated PDF)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy.park@orchardai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchardai.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft renewal and capacity increase — proposal attached

Amy, Jordan — looping in a note from the deal desk. Given Orchard's growth and long-term strategic fit, we recommend two concessions to close the renewal quickly: 

1) Waive first-month overage fees during the migration window (30 days from term start) to reduce migration risk.
2) Price protection for the first 3 months of the term (no price increases tied to minor model upgrades).

We will also include a short SLA appendix with a p99 option: p99 < 150ms at committed throughput; if Orchard opts into the p99 guarantee we will require a 7.5% premium on the net monthly commit. The amendment attached reflects those options.

If legal needs redlines, send them back to me and I'll coordinate with our counsel.

–Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: orchard-capacity-amendment-v3.pdf (sales-redline)]

From: Amy Park <amy.park@orchardai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchardai.com, legal@orchardai.com
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft renewal and capacity increase — proposal attached

Thanks, Marissa and Jordan — that direction is helpful. Orchard is willing to move forward in principle with the 16-GPU reserved pool under these conditions: 

- We accept the waived first-month overage and 3-month price protection.
- We'll take the p99 appendix as an optional add-on. Please provide final wording so legal can sign off quickly.
- We expect the committed term to start 2027-01-01; please confirm the provisioning timeline so we can schedule our deploys.
- Please provide a DocuSign link with the updated monetary terms and credit applied to the first invoice.

If we have the final package by EOD 12/03 we can route to our CFO for signature.

Regards,
Amy Park
Head of Infrastructure | Orchard AI
amy.park@orchardai.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy.park@orchardai.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, procurement@orchardai.com, legal@orchardai.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft renewal and capacity increase — proposal attached

Amy — great, appreciate the quick turn. Final recap and next steps: 

1) Financials: 16 GPU reserved pool, $86,400/month net; one-time 10% credit applied to first invoice (as discussed). DocuSign with updated amounts is here: https://www.docusign.com/seed/ORCH-3421 (internal link)
2) SLA: we'll include an appendix with p95 by default; p99 < 150ms is available as an opt-in for +7.5% monthly premium. Redlines attached for legal review.
3) Provisioning: we will begin reserved pool provisioning on 2026-12-15 to meet the 2027-01-01 start date. Provisioning plan in the attached spreadsheet details the steps and runbook owner.
4) Migration relief: first 30 days waiver on overage charges; 3-month price protection on net commit.

Next steps for Orchard: send confirmation to sign by EOD 12/03 if you want us to route the DocuSign envelope to your CFO. Once signed we'll schedule the kickoff and provisioning call (30–45 min).

Thanks — I'll stand by for the signed DocuSign.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]
[Attachment: orchard-capacity-amendment-v3.pdf (final redline)]
